remediation.issue: Examples use connection strings and account URLs from environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use managed identity or a secret manager where available, and grant the smallest required Azure Files permissions.

remediation.issue: The download example writes a file to a fixed local path.
remediation.suggestion: Make the destination explicit, validate it, and avoid overwriting existing files without user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Cloud file operations can access sensitive share data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit account and share selection, use least-privilege credentials, and document data-handling expectations.

content.user_title: Manage Azure File Shares in Python
content.value_statement: Teams often need reliable Python code for Azure Files shares, directories, and file transfers. This skill gives ready patterns for authentication, listing, upload, download, copy, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Install the Azure Storage File Share Python package and set connection or identity-based credentials.
Create and manage file shares, directories, and files with the official Azure clients.
Upload, download, copy, rename, and delete files in Azure Files.
List share contents and inspect file or directory properties.
Handle large files with streaming and chunked transfers.
Use SAS tokens or DefaultAzureCredential for scoped access.
limitations: This skill documents the Python SDK. It does not provision Azure resources or manage access policies for you.
It does not replace Azure portal, CLI, or ARM templates for infrastructure setup.
Examples assume a valid Azure Files account, share, and credentials already exist.
It does not cover NFS shares, Storage Explorer workflows, or non-Python clients.

use_cases.title: Automate report delivery
use_cases.description: A backend engineer uploads generated reports to a share and later downloads them for processing.

use_cases.title: Organize shared project files
use_cases.description: A DevOps engineer creates directories, lists files, and removes stale artifacts from a team share.

use_cases.title: Move files between shares
use_cases.description: A data engineer copies source files to another Azure Files path before a batch job starts.

prompt_templates.title: Connect and list a share
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Azure Storage File Share Python SDK to connect with my environment credentials and list the files in share reports.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a first working list operation.

prompt_templates.title: Upload a local file
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Python that creates directory exports if needed and uploads ./daily.csv to Azure Files share reports as exports/daily.csv.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application needs a repeatable upload path.

prompt_templates.title: Download and inspect a file
prompt_templates.prompt: Download reports/exports/daily.csv from Azure Files, save it locally, and print the file properties after the transfer.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operator wants to retrieve one file and confirm metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Copy, rename, and clean up
prompt_templates.prompt: Using DefaultAzureCredential, copy source.txt to archive/source.txt, rename the copy, stream a large file in chunks, then delete the original only after a successful copy.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced workflow needs copy, rename, streaming, and safe deletion.

output_examples.input: List the files in Azure Files share reports.
output_examples.output: The skill returns Python that connects with your configured credentials, opens the reports share, and prints each file and directory name.

output_examples.input: Upload daily.csv to reports/exports and then download it.
output_examples.output: The skill creates the exports directory if needed, uploads the local file, then writes the downloaded content to a named local file.

output_examples.input: Copy a large file between two Azure Files paths without loading it all into memory.
output_examples.output: The skill shows a start-copy flow and a chunked stream so the file moves in parts instead of one large in-memory buffer.

best_practices: Store account URLs and secrets in environment variables or a secret manager. Do not hardcode them.
Use DefaultAzureCredential or a narrowly scoped SAS token instead of a full account key when possible.
Stream large files in chunks and confirm successful copies before deleting source files.
anti_patterns: Do not commit connection strings, account keys, or SAS tokens into source control.
Do not download large files into memory when a chunked stream is available.
Do not delete or overwrite share files without confirming the target path and a successful copy.

faq.question: Which Python package does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the official azure-storage-file-share package and the matching Azure Files client classes.

faq.question: How should I authenticate?
faq.answer: Use a connection string, account URL plus credential, DefaultAzureCredential, or a SAS token stored outside source code.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new file share?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to create a share and then work with directories and files inside that share.

faq.question: Does it support large file transfers?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes chunked streaming so large files do not need to load fully into memory.

faq.question: Can I copy files between Azure Files paths?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes start-copy examples for moving a file from one share path to another.

faq.question: Does this provision Azure infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. You still need an existing storage account, share permissions, and credentials before running the examples.
